description:
We are a global team of innovators and pioneers dedicated to shaping the future of observability. At New Relic, we build an intelligent platform that empowers companies to thrive in an AI-first world by giving them unparalleled insight into their complex systems. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we're looking for passionate people to join our mission. If you're ready to help the world's best companies optimize their digital applications, we invite you to explore a career with us!
 About the Team 
 The NR Lens team builds New Relic's Federated Data Platform — a distributed SQL query engine that lets customers connect external data sources (Snowflake, PostgreSQL, Google Sheets, AWS CloudWatch) and query them directly from New Relic.
 You'll work on the distributed query execution layer, connector architecture, and API gateway that powers cross-source JOINs and unified analytics across customer data stores.
   What You'll Do 
 Design, build, and maintain cloud-native Java microservices in the NR Lens query path: SQL Gateway, Query Gateway, and data source connector plugins
 Develop and harden JDBC connector integrations — including connection lifecycle management, credential handling, query pushdown optimization, and security validation
 Improve query reliability and performance across a multi-tenant distributed SQL deployment serving 50+ customers
 Build and operate services on AWS (EKS, IAM/STS, S3) with infrastructure-as-code practices
 Implement security controls for user-supplied connection parameters (JDBC URL validation, SSRF prevention, hostname allowlisting)
 Build materialized view scheduling, execution, and lifecycle management features
 Design and implement deployment automation — canary deployments, progressive rollouts, observability integration
 Collaborate with the NRDB/Dirac team on the internal connector bridging federated queries to New Relic's native telemetry engine
 Participate in on-call rotation and incident response for production systems
   What We're Looking For 
   Must Have: 
 5+ years of professional Java development .
 Strong experience building cloud-native applications on AWS.
 Experience designing and operating containerized microservices on Kubernetes
 Experience building and operating distributed systems at scale
 Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and CI/CD pipelines
 Experience with AWS security patterns.
 Experience with observability tooling — defining SLOs/SLIs, dashboards, alerting
 Comfort debugging production issues across multi-service architectures
 Experience with gRPC or Thrift-based service communication
 Experience with GraphQL APIs
   Nice to Have: 
 Strong understanding of SQL query execution — parsing, planning, optimization, or execution engines
 Experience with JDBC drivers, connection pooling, and database connector development
 Experience with distributed query engines or SQL-on-anything platforms
 Experience developing plugins or connectors for distributed query engines (SPI-based architectures)
 Knowledge of RBAC/authorization systems in multi-tenant SaaS environments
 Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
 Fostering a diverse, welcoming and inclusive environment is important to us. We work hard to make everyone feel comfortable bringing their best, most authentic selves to work every day. We celebrate our talented Relics’ different backgrounds and abilities, and recognize the different paths they took to reach us – including nontraditional ones. Their experiences and perspectives inspire us to make our products and company the best they can be. We’re looking for people who feel connected to our mission and values, not just candidates who check off all the boxes. 
 If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application or recruiting process, please reach out to resume@newrelic.com .
 We believe in empowering all Relics to achieve professional and business success through a flexible workforce model. This model allows us to work in a variety of workplaces that best support our success, including fully office-based, fully remote, or hybrid.
 Our hiring process 
In compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work and to complete employment eligibility verification. Note: Our stewardship of the data of thousands of customers means that a criminal background check is required to join New Relic.
We will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records based on individual circumstances and in accordance with applicable law including, but not limited to, the  San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance .
Headhunters and recruitment agencies may not submit resumes/CVs through this website or directly to managers. New Relic does not accept unsolicited headhunter and agency resumes, and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with New Relic.
 New Relic develops and distributes encryption software and technology that complies with U.S. export controls and licensing requirements. Certain New Relic roles require candidates to pass an export compliance assessment as a condition of employment in any global location. If relevant, we will provide more information later in the application process.
 Candidates are evaluated based on qualifications, regardless of race, religion, ethnicity, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, age, disability, neurodiversity, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other legally protected characteristics. 
 Review our Applicant Privacy Notice at  https://newrelic.com/termsandconditions/applicant-privacy-policy

About the team

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.

The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.

About the role

You keep the infrastructure behind Sarvam’s products running. You handle day-to-day operations — deployments, provisioning, access, incidents and cost questions — and you are expected to automate that work away.

We hire for one instinct above everything else: you notice something done by hand every day, ask why it can’t run itself, and build the thing that removes it — a script, a pipeline step, a bot, a small Kubernetes operator, or an AI agent that does the work. Operations is a large part of this role, and it is where you find what is worth automating.

As you automate your own toil away, more of your time goes into platform and automation work.

Products you may work on

Sarvam builds across a broad range of AI products: voice agents, coding agents, coworker agents, dubbing, our API platform, and the real-time voice and WebRTC infrastructure underneath them, among many others. You will work on the infrastructure behind them.

Responsibilities

• Own infrastructure operations across Sarvam’s products: deployments, provisioning requests, access, environment issues, cost questions

• Respond to incidents, write the runbook or postmortem afterwards, and fix the cause

• Automate repeated work: turn manual steps into pipeline jobs, Terraform modules, templates or self-service for product teams

• Build AI-assisted automations: agents that triage alerts, summarise incidents, review routine changes or answer product teams’ infrastructure questions, with a human approving anything risky

• Security basics: keep images and dependencies patched, rotate credentials, keep secrets out of code, fix security findings

• Reliability basics: keep dashboards and alerts accurate, track SLOs and cost, delete noisy alerts

• Take part in on-call

Requirements

• 2–5 years in DevOps, SRE, infrastructure or backend engineering

• Has built infrastructure outside a ticket: a homelab, an open-source contribution, a side project, or an internal tool nobody asked for — and can show the code (GitHub, a blog post or a demo)

• Comfortable on the Linux command line: processes, networking basics, logs, systemd

• Working knowledge of Docker and Kubernetes; has deployed and debugged something running on a cluster

• Scripting in Python, Go or Bash

• Basic Git and CI/CD experience

• Has spotted a repeated manual task — a daily review, a recurring fix, a routine request — and built something that removed it: a script, a CI job, a bot or a Kubernetes operator. You can walk us through what you noticed, why it mattered, what you built and what it saved

• Has used LLMs or AI agents to automate real work, not only for writing code

• Fixes causes rather than the same symptom twice; asks “why is this manual?” before doing it again

• Curious, takes ownership, wants to grow into platform engineering

• Nice to have: Terraform, a public cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP), Prometheus / Grafana, exposure to SIP, WebRTC or real-time media, any cloud or Kubernetes certification

description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior ML Engineer - Malware Detection based remotely in India. 
 The Senior ML Engineer will develop and deploy advanced machine learning solutions to detect web-based malware across large-scale Linux hosting environments. Working with an extensive dataset of real-world malware samples, analyst decisions, detection rules, and cleanup outcomes, you will transform production intelligence into more accurate and efficient security systems. Your work will span classical machine learning, transformer models, LLM-assisted triage, and automated signature generation. You will own the journey from raw data and experimentation to production deployment, with success measured by real detection improvements and controlled false-positive rates. Collaborating closely with malware analysts, infrastructure specialists, and fellow ML engineers, you will have access to dedicated GPU resources and modern AI-assisted development tools. This remote-first opportunity is ideal for an experienced ML practitioner who thrives on experimentation, rigorous evaluation, and delivering measurable cybersecurity impact.
Accountabilities:
You will lead the development, evaluation, and deployment of machine learning systems that improve malware detection at scale while balancing accuracy, operational costs, and resource constraints. Your key responsibilities will include:
 Machine Learning Model Development: Design, train, fine-tune, and deploy ML models using production malware data to improve detection coverage and identify threats that traditional signatures and rules may miss.
 Malware Classification and Triage: Develop models that distinguish malicious files from benign content, prioritize suspicious files for deeper inspection, and route samples to the most appropriate detection engines.
 Automated Signature Generation: Build systems that generate detection signatures from emerging malware campaigns, helping security analysts respond faster to new and evolving threats.
 Context-Aware Threat Detection: Develop methods to identify malicious content that requires contextual analysis, including phishing pages, webshells, script injections, and compromised website components.
 Detection and Cleanup Optimization: Improve detection precision and cleanup effectiveness so that infected websites remain clean after remediation and recurring threats can be identified.
 Model Evaluation and Validation: Establish rigorous evaluation frameworks using time-based and campaign-based dataset splits, historical false-positive and false-negative cases, and regression testing to prevent data leakage and verify improvements before deployment.
 Inference and Resource Optimization: Optimize model throughput, latency, CPU usage, memory consumption, and cost per file to support reliable deployment across large hosting fleets.
 Production Deployment and Monitoring: Move models from experimentation into production, using shadow deployments and controlled releases to gather evidence before enabling live detection.
 Continuous Learning and Retraining: Incorporate fresh analyst feedback and newly identified false negatives into training datasets, establish regular retraining cycles, and monitor trends in detection rates and model performance.
 ML Infrastructure and Experimentation: Develop reusable training pipelines, maintain dataset tooling, make effective use of GPU resources, and enable multiple parallel research and development efforts.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with malware analysts, detection engineers, and infrastructure teams to investigate customer-reported detection failures, understand emerging threats, and translate operational findings into model improvements.
 Technical Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Document architectural decisions, evaluation methods, model limitations, hardware requirements, and production results. Participate in asynchronous collaboration and blameless post-mortems to continuously improve engineering practices.
 Delivery Against Milestones: Train and evaluate an initial production-data model during the first month, bring multiple models into production or shadow testing by month three, and help establish ML as a major source of new detections within the first year.
 Requirements: 
 The ideal candidate combines substantial production ML experience with hands-on transformer expertise, strong evaluation discipline, and the ability to engineer efficient models for adversarial security environments. You should be comfortable making evidence-based decisions, communicating asynchronously, and taking ownership of the full ML lifecycle. Key qualifications include:
 Production ML Experience: At least five years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production, including at least two years in an adversarial domain such as cybersecurity, fraud, spam, or abuse prevention.
 Transformer Model Expertise: Practical experience training and fine-tuning transformer models, including data preparation, code tokenization, LoRA/QLoRA or full fine-tuning, distillation, and quantization. Experience should extend beyond calling hosted model APIs.
 Classical Machine Learning: Strong understanding of gradient boosting, linear models with sparse features, probability calibration, class imbalance, and the ability to determine when traditional ML methods outperform LLM-based approaches.
 Rigorous Model Evaluation: Experience designing leakage-free splits by time and malware family, evaluating precision under fixed false-positive constraints, maintaining regression datasets, and understanding the limitations of offline evaluation when predicting production performance.
 Inference and Cost Optimization: Demonstrated ability to measure throughput and latency and optimize models for CPU, memory, and operational cost constraints. Familiarity with technologies such as ONNX, llama.cpp, vLLM, and int8/int4 quantization is valuable.
 Technical Stack: Strong Python, PyTorch, and Hugging Face skills, along with SQL expertise for analyzing large datasets using ClickHouse or comparable analytical databases.
 Web Technology Familiarity: Experience with PHP or JavaScript, or a willingness to learn these technologies while collaborating with malware analysts.
 AI-Assisted Engineering: Daily use of AI coding agents, with the ability to demonstrate how they support development, investigation, and engineering productivity.
 Written Communication: English proficiency at B2 level or higher, with particularly strong written communication skills for technical documentation and asynchronous collaboration.
 Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to investigate complex detection problems, interpret model results, make sound technical trade-offs, and prioritize measurable improvements over experimental metrics alone.
 Ownership and Collaboration: Comfort taking responsibility from experimentation through production deployment while working effectively with analysts, engineers, and other stakeholders.
 The following experience would be a strong advantage:
 Web Malware Security: Experience with web malware, webshells, phishing kits, or WordPress security.
 Code-Based Machine Learning: Experience developing models over source code using abstract syntax trees (ASTs), token features, code-focused language models, or graph models of program structure.
 Malware Analysis: Knowledge of malware clustering, similarity analysis, and methods for identifying related samples or emerging campaigns.
 Training Infrastructure: Experience with multi-GPU training on bare-metal infrastructure, MLflow or Weights & Biases, and dataset versioning.
 Systems Programming: Familiarity with Go or Rust for efficient on-server inference.
 Security Research: Published work, technical presentations, or conference talks focused on machine learning for cybersecurity.
 Benefits: 
 Fully Remote Work: Work remotely with flexibility to organize your schedule and work from different locations worldwide, subject to hiring arrangements.
 Flexible Working Hours: Autonomy to structure your working day in a remote-first, asynchronous environment.
 Paid Vacation: 24 days of paid vacation annually.
 Public Holidays: 10 days of national holidays.
 Sick Leave: Unlimited sick leave.

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. About the role

You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.

Responsibilities

• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds

• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency

• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys

• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks

• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest

• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails

• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs

• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team

• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes

• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents

Requirements

• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment

• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud

• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)

• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines

• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds

• Scripting and tooling in Python or Go

• Has been through security audits and knows what evidence auditors need

• Has built or used AI-based automation in infrastructure or security work, and understands the risks of AI agents: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, unreviewed actions

• Nice to have: Vault, SPIFFE / SPIRE, Falco or Tetragon, Cloudflare WAF, incident response lead experience, multi-cloud experience
